scenes.text: Your body actually glows in the dark, just too faintly to see.
In two thousand nine, Japanese scientists filmed people in total darkness with ultra-sensitive cameras.
The light was about one thousand times weaker than our eyes can detect.
The glow was brightest around four in the afternoon and dimmest around ten in the morning.
Faces glowed the most, possibly helped by skin pigment.
Scientists think the light comes from chemical reactions in your metabolism.
Would you want to see people glowing?

title: Your body glows in the dark (you just can't see it) ✨
caption: In a 2009 study, Japanese researchers filmed people's faint natural glow with ultra-sensitive cameras. It's about 1,000 times too weak for our eyes and peaks around 4 p.m. ✨
